cats.d: Foam it, wash it, or skip the hose entirely — plus the ceramic layer that goes on after.
Brake dust off, sidewalls back to black, nothing slung down the side of your car.
Dash, console, trim and cabin air. Clean finishes, no gloss, no greasy film.
The microfiber, brushes, cannons and buckets the chemistry was built around.
Golf carts, boats and anything that comes home covered in trail dust.
Start with one bottle or take the whole bay. Every system is a real discount on the parts.

products.title: LuxPro — Waterless Wash
products.line: Skip the hose. Keep the shine.
products.short: Nano-polymers wrap the dust so it lifts off the paint instead of dragging across it. No bucket, no hose, no driveway.
products.desc: LuxPro is the bottle NanoFusion was built for. Advanced nano-polymers encapsulate light dust, pollen, fingerprints and road film so they lift away from the surface rather than getting dragged across it, while a high-lubricity carrier keeps the towel gliding. What stays behind is a slick, hydrophobic layer that adds gloss, tightens water beading and keeps the next round of dust from taking hold. It is the difference between wiping a car down and actually cleaning it.
how: Shake well before each use.
Work one panel at a time, out of direct sun.
Mist a light, even coat onto the surface.
Wipe in one direction with a clean Edgeless Lux towel.
Flip to a dry side and buff off the haze.

products.title: CeramicX — Ceramic Spray
products.line: Bonded protection, one panel at a time.
products.short: A ceramic layer in the time it takes to wipe a panel. Hard water beading, real gloss depth, and a surface that stays clean longer.
products.desc: CeramicX bonds to the surface and leaves a durable, hydrophobic layer that repels water, road grime and UV. Gloss goes up, dirt has less to grab, and the next wash takes half as long. It layers on top of a coating you already have rather than replacing it, so it works as both a standalone protectant and a topper between full ceramic services.
how: Start with a clean, dry, cool surface.
Mist two to three sprays per panel.
Spread evenly with an Edgeless Lux towel.
Flip to a dry towel and buff until it disappears.
Give it an hour before it sees rain.
products.coverage: 10–20 vehicles per bottle · up to 8 months of protection

products.title: LuxFoam — Foam Soap
products.line: Let the foam do the scrubbing.
products.short: Thick, clinging foam that lifts the grit before your mitt ever touches the paint — the single biggest thing standing between a wash and a swirl.
products.desc: LuxFoam throws rich foam that clings long enough to actually break down road film instead of sliding straight off. High lubricity means the mitt glides rather than grabs, and dirt stays encapsulated in the suds where it cannot cut into the clear coat. It rinses clean with no residue and will not strip the wax, sealant or coating already on the car.
how: Rinse the car down first — never foam a dry, dusty panel.
Fill the cannon and dial in a thick mix.
Blanket the vehicle top to bottom and let it dwell.
Wash with a LuxMit, top panels first, rinsing the mitt often.
Rinse fully and dry with a LuxTowel.

products.title: LuxWheelAssassin — Wheel Cleaner
products.line: Attack the brake dust. Leave the finish alone.
products.short: Fast-acting on bonded brake dust, grease and road film, so the barrel comes clean with a fraction of the scrubbing.
products.desc: Brake dust is not dirt — it is hot metal fused into your finish, and scrubbing it is how wheels get ruined. LuxWheelAssassin breaks it down chemically so it releases with minimal agitation, then rinses away clean. Safe on clear-coated, painted, chrome, alloy and factory wheels, which covers virtually everything short of bare polished aluminium.
how: Work on cool wheels, out of direct sun.
Spray the face and the barrel until wet.
Let it dwell — do not let it dry.
Agitate with a Lux Wheel Brush where buildup is heavy.
Rinse thoroughly, then dry before dressing the tires.
products.note: Always test an inconspicuous area first.

products.title: TireVenom — Tire Dressing
products.line: Deep black that stays on the tire.
products.short: A no-sling dressing that dries to the touch. Even, dark sidewalls — and none of it flung down your paint on the first pull-out.
products.desc: Most tire shine is silicone that never really dries, which is why it ends up in a stripe along your rocker panel. TireVenom dries to the touch and stays where you put it. It restores faded rubber to a deep, even finish and shields it against UV, cracking and browning, without the greasy film that attracts dust the moment you park.
how: Scrub the sidewall clean first — dressing over old dressing is what causes browning.
Let the tire dry completely.
Apply an even coat with an XPad applicator.
Level it out so there are no heavy spots.
Let it set before you drive.
products.coverage: 30–50 tires per bottle · up to 3 months

products.title: InteriorX — Interior Cleaner
products.line: Clean cabin. No gloss, no glare.
products.short: Lifts fingerprints, spills and everyday grime off dash, console and door cards — then leaves, with no slick residue and nothing reflecting in your windshield.
products.desc: Interior cleaner is the easiest place to make a car look worse. Anything that leaves shine puts glare in your windshield and turns your steering wheel slippery. InteriorX pulls dirt, dust, fingerprints and spills off the surface and dries to a factory matte, so the cabin reads clean rather than coated.
how: Spray onto a MicroLux towel, not directly onto the panel.
Work one section at a time.
Wipe, then follow with a dry side of the towel.
Use a LuxBrush for vents, seams and switchgear.

Wipe and follow with a dry side.

products.desc: Faded grey trim is what makes a clean car still look old. It levels out rather than sitting on top, so nothing feels greasy and nothing collects dust.
how: Clean and dry the surface first.
Apply a thin coat with an XPad applicator.
Let it level for a minute.
Wipe back any excess with a dry towel.

One short burst into the vents with the fan running.
